title: Treasury International Capital (TIC) monthly release (July 2026 data) + the quarterly cut, 4:00 p.m. ET
source: TSY: two independent treasury.gov primaries, both fetched direct by this event's own initial-research session 2026-09-08 (plain curl, HTTP 200). (1) The June-2026 TIC press release (home.treasury.gov/news/press-releases/sb0606) states verbatim 'The next release, which will report on data for July 2026, is scheduled for September 16, 2026.' (2) home.treasury.gov/data/treasury-international-capital-tic-system/release-dates-of-tic-data puts September's monthly release AND the quarterly cut ('nonfinancial firms, derivatives, portfolio claims and liabilities at end of previous quarter') both on the 16th, with the gross-external-debt cut separately on the 30th, under the page header 'All data releases occur at 4 p.m. Washington, D.C. time'. Reference month July 2026 by the page's own stated 1.5-month lag, and named as such by the press release. PROMOTED from estimate 2026-09-08 on the mts-october-2026-11-12 precedent, item for item: the original estimate grounds were this lane's no-self-confirm limit (the entry was discovered in the import-export-prices-2026-09-16 adjacency sweep, not researched), and that is cleared — this session re-fetched both primaries independently, and TSY: is an authorized confirmed-tier prefix. The prefix gloss in market-events-data.ts reads 'treasury.gov / treasurydirect.gov auction schedule'; this is a treasury.gov RELEASE schedule, the same extension mts-august-2026-09-11 and mts-october-2026-11-12 already made and recorded. Third corroboration, mechanical and independent of both pages: the release-dates page's own published rule is 'the 11th business day plus 0 to 3 days', and the 11th business day of September 2026 is the 15th once Labor Day 09-07 is excluded, so the rule permits 09-15 through 09-18 and the published date sits inside it. Checked 2026-09-08
notes: The calendar's only capital-account print: who finances the deficit, measured directly. Value is as a monthly structural gauge, NOT a tradeable date — 16:00 ET is after the equity cash close, on the single most crowded macro day of the month (fomc-2026-09-16 decides at 14:00, presser 14:30), reporting data that is six weeks stale. No house playbook is macro-keyed and symbols is empty; nothing here licenses an entry. What it measures, from the last released month (June 2026, published 2026-08-17): foreign Treasury holdings $9,299.0bn, down $72.1bn m/m and $190.4bn off February's $9,489.4bn record — but foreigners were NET BUYERS of long-term Treasuries that month (+$6.8bn) and foreign official net inflows were +$48.4bn, so the fall was mark-to-market plus bill runoff, not a buyer strike. The composition is the real signal: of $207.1bn foreign net purchases of US long-term securities in June, equities took $181.4bn and Treasuries $6.8bn, with agencies at -$16.8bn. On the July data this release carries, the 10Y rose 31bp (4.44% -> 4.75% month-end), and a valuation model fit on 41 months (R^2 0.95, implied duration 4.16) puts the long-term Treasury valuation change at about -$95bn, so headline holdings will very likely fall again and the 'foreigners are dumping Treasuries' read of that fall will again be mostly wrong. Read for_lt_treas_net in slt_table3, never the holdings delta. Discovered in the import-export-prices-2026-09-16 adjacency sweep; researched and date-promoted by its own session 2026-09-08.
